title: Playing at white funerals
summary: Laine's band played a regular march at funerals; Allen notes fraternal organizations were expected to have bands.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Now, we used to play pretty good marches. It was one march we played. Can't think of the name of that march now. Well, anyhow, we used to play it. We played it regular so people would know just the stuff we played. For every funeral, we played it regular. You played at funerals?
Oh, Lord, yes. They had bands at white funerals? Yes. Is that right? Oh, yes. I played many funerals. Is that right?

You can tell you that. Well, did they have bands at white funerals when you were a child, when you were a little boy? Yes. Is that right? Yes. When did they stop doing that? When did they stop doing that? When did they stop having bands at white funerals? I wouldn't know. Well, they never have stopped. They always have been military funerals. I never know. Well, I mean, yeah. I wouldn't know. It was a rule, Papa, for all organizations to at that time. I see. All the fraternal organizations throughout the country. It was a rule for all organizations that time to have bands.
Oh, yes. I reckon so. I wouldn't know that.
